split_note: 4-for-1 stock split effective July 2, 2026 (record date June 25, 2026). All per-share figures in this model use the PRE-SPLIT share count (257.9M diluted) and PRE-SPLIT price ($701.09) to remain consistent with the currently quoted market price. Post-split equivalent: divide intrinsic values and current price by 4.

inputs.cash_definition: Cash & equivalents per Q1 FY2027 balance sheet (quarter ended April 30, 2026). Prior model used FY2025 year-end cash; updated to most recent quarter per convention of using latest available balance sheet data.

historical_growth.growth_divergence_warning: Equity CAGR (44.3% 3yr, 38.7% 5yr) is distorted by low post-IPO book value base and GAAP losses masking retained earnings — not used as primary rate. EPS CAGRs not calculable due to persistent GAAP losses through FY2026 (net loss $162.5M FY2026). Revenue 3yr CAGR (29.0%) diverges from FCF 3yr CAGR (22.4%) by 6.6pp — within tolerance but reflects FCF margins stabilizing around 25-27%. FCF 3yr CAGR (22.4%) selected as primary anchor as it aligns with ARR-implied growth and management guidance of ~23-24% revenue growth in FY2027. Near-term growth moderated to 22% (Y1), consistent with ARR guidance, then decelerated toward terminal.

base.description: Steady execution on FY2027 guidance (~23-24% revenue growth). ARR growth at 24%, decelerating as law of large numbers sets in. FCF margins improve from ~25.8% in FY2026 toward ~27% as S&M leverage partially offsets AI investment. Growth decelerates from 22% to 12% by Y5.

bull.description: AI DR acceleration (250% sequential growth continues), Falcon Flex Re-Flex flywheel drives above-consensus ARR growth, Charlotte AI AgentWorks creates premium upsell layer. Revenue growth re-accelerates to 26-28% range in FY2027-28. FCF margins expand to 30%+ as platform leverage scales. $20B ARR aspiration begins to look achievable on schedule.

bear.description: Microsoft competitive pressure intensifies in mid-market and SIEM; Delta litigation results in large adverse judgment (~$300-500M settlement). ARR growth decelerates to mid-teens. FCF margins compress as elevated S&M spend fails to reaccelerate growth and integration costs from SGNL/Seraphic weigh on margins.

sensitivity.note: Base scenario. Rows = WACC (8-12%), Columns = Terminal Growth (2.0-4.0%). Values are intrinsic value per share in USD (pre-split).

probability_weighted.note: Probability-weighted IV of $148.27 reflects CrowdStrike's strong platform position and accelerating ARR, offset by extreme starting multiple ($701/share), 5-year DCF horizon limitation, and execution risks from multiple simultaneous integrations. At $701/share the stock requires sustained above-consensus growth well beyond the 5-year window to justify current price.

sanity_check.warning_message: VALUATION GAP — 5-YEAR DCF UNDERSTATES PREMIUM GROWTH PLATFORM VALUE
sanity_check.detail: TRIPPED. Market EV/FCF of 149x and EV/ARR of 33.5x are at the top of (and slightly above) CRWD's historical trading range, confirming the market prices in a long, high-growth runway that a standard 5-year DCF cannot fully capture. The base DCF IV ($143.21/share pre-split) implies an EV/FCF of only 27x — roughly 5.6x below the market multiple. This is structurally expected for a premium SaaS platform with 24% ARR growth, 97% gross retention, and a credible $20B ARR aspiration. The 5-year DCF should be treated as a floor/downside anchor. A longer-dated model (10yr) or ARR-based NAV would bridge the gap. Note: EV/ARR of 33.5x is slightly above the historical 15-30x range, suggesting the market is pricing in some AI DR / AgentWorks optionality premium beyond core ARR compounding.
sanity_check.recommended_framework: For CRWD, complement the 5-year DCF with: (1) ARR-based NAV: terminal ARR x NTM revenue multiple, (2) 10-year FCF model extending growth to FY2031+, (3) Reverse DCF to determine what growth rate the current price implies.

valuation_philosophy.approach: FCF-based 5-year DCF with terminal perpetuity growth
valuation_philosophy.primary_metric: Free Cash Flow (not GAAP earnings, which are distorted by $700M+ annual SBC)
valuation_philosophy.growth_anchor: FCF 3-year CAGR (22.4%) calibrated against FY2027 ARR guidance (24% growth) and management's $20B ARR by FY2036 long-term target (~14% CAGR from $5.25B)
valuation_philosophy.equity_cagr_exclusion: Equity/Book Value CAGR explicitly NOT used as the standard system recommends, per user instructions and MEMORY.md: for high-growth SaaS with GAAP losses, equity CAGR is meaningless. FCF CAGR is the appropriate anchor.
limitations: 5-year DCF structurally undervalues long-duration compounders like CRWD where the bulk of value resides in years 6-20
Terminal value sensitivity is extreme at high growth + low WACC combinations
Does not capture ARR optionality from AI DR, AgentWorks, or new platform pillars
SBC dilution (~$700M/yr) is not explicitly deducted from FCF projections — FCF is reported after capex but before SBC
valuation_philosophy.sbc_note: CrowdStrike's reported FCF does not deduct stock-based compensation (~$700M in FY2026, ~$727M estimated FY2027). On an SBC-adjusted basis, true owner earnings are materially lower. At 257.9M diluted shares, $700M SBC equals ~$2.72/share annual dilution cost not reflected in FCF-based IV.

valuation_commentary.summary: CrowdStrike's DCF intrinsic value of $143.21 (base), $215.13 (bull), and $91.54 (bear) reflects the structural tension between excellent operational momentum and a $701/share pre-split price (~$181B market cap). FY2026 demonstrated record $1.24B FCF, ARR surpassing $5.25B at 24% growth, and the company's first GAAP-profitable quarter. Q1 FY2027 extended the streak with record $469M quarterly FCF and ARR accelerating to $5.51B. The market is pricing in a premium for AI DR optionality, the Falcon Flex flywheel, and the $20B ARR aspiration — none of which are captured in a standard 5-year DCF. At current prices, investors are effectively paying for the full bull case and more.
valuation_commentary.key_assumptions_sensitivity: Base IV is highly sensitive to terminal growth and WACC. At 8% WACC / 4% terminal growth (aggressive but not irrational for a market-leading SaaS platform), IV reaches $237. The current price of $701 implies either: (a) a WACC well below 8% reflecting index-level demand for premium growth, (b) a terminal growth rate above 4%, or (c) an extended high-growth window (10+ year DCF) that yields substantially higher values.
valuation_commentary.outage_impact: The July 2024 Falcon outage risk is substantially diminished as evidenced by FY2026 net new ARR of $1.01B (+47%) and Q1 FY2027 net new ARR of $256M (+32%). Delta Air Lines litigation ($500M+ claim, gross negligence allowed to proceed) remains the primary unresolved tail risk, reflected in the bear case discount rate (12% WACC) and lower growth assumptions.
valuation_commentary.split_context: The 4-for-1 stock split effective July 2, 2026 is value-neutral. Post-split equivalent intrinsic values: base $35.80, bull $53.78, bear $22.89. Post-split equivalent current price: ~$175.27.
valuation_commentary.recommended_entry_zone: Value investors requiring a 15% CAGR to terminal value would need to purchase at $78 (base) to $125 (bull) — pre-split — to achieve that return target. The current $701 implies the market accepts a far lower required return (~5-6% to terminal value) or expects growth compounding well beyond the 5-year projection window.
